newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power steady to up on cold, natgas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power steady to up on cold, natgas.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast were steady to slightly higher Monday as traders anticipated cooler air to arrive late this week and natural gas prices rose sharply.

Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to gradually cool throughout this week before a blast of cold air arrives late Friday or early Saturday, pushing temperatures to about 10 degrees Fahrenheit below-normal.

Firm, peak power prices in the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Tuesday were assessed mostly steady in the $17.00-20.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, as compared with Friday's $18.00-19.00 trading range.
Firm, off-peak electricity in northern TVA for Tuesday was still around $13.00 per MWh, traders said.
At the Georgia/Florida border, prices for firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks for Tuesday delivery were talked in the $24.00-25.00 range, up an average of $2 from Friday's levels.
Firm, off-peak power for Tuesday at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally at $16.00-17.00.

In Florida, where daytime temperatures are reaching highs of 70s and 80s and lows of 50s and 60s, firm, peak electricity prices on a 16-hour schedule for Tuesday were also higher around $26.00 per MWh.
Helping to support electricity prices was the significantly stronger natural gas market. Gas prices along the Gulf Coast rose more than $1 to the $3.44-3.49 per million British thermal units area.
Separately, Texas Utilities shut its 1,150 megawatt Comanche 2 nuclear power unit in Glen Rose, Texas. The company said it expected to restart the unit late Tuesday or early Wednesday.
